faq.q: Does my Word file get uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The .docx is opened with JavaScript in this tab, laid out into pages here, and the PDF is built here with pdf-lib. The page loads its libraries and the free fonts it uses from public CDNs, but your document is never sent anywhere. You can disconnect from the internet after the page has loaded and convert a file.

faq.q: Why can the PDF have a different number of pages than Word?
faq.a: Word decides where each page ends using its own text engine and the fonts installed on your computer. This tool lays the text out again in the browser. Calibri, Cambria, Arial, Times New Roman and Courier New are swapped for free fonts with the same letter widths (Carlito, Caladea, Arimo, Tinos, Cousine), so lines usually break in the same places, but a page can still end a few lines earlier or later. The file box shows Word's own page count so you can compare.

faq.q: Can I search or copy text in the converted PDF?
faq.a: Yes, when 'Make text selectable & searchable' is ticked. Each page is stored as a picture, and an invisible text layer is placed over it line by line, so Ctrl+F and copy work. That layer uses a standard PDF font, so it covers English and other Latin-script text; Hindi and other Devanagari text is visible in the PDF but is not searchable.

faq.q: Which Word features are not converted?
faq.a: Charts, SmartArt and old EMF/WMF images are not drawn, and text boxes are placed only approximately. Comments are left out and tracked changes are shown as accepted. The table of contents keeps the page numbers Word last saved. The tool tells you in the notes under the Convert button when your file contains any of these. Old .doc files (Word 97–2003) must be saved as .docx first.
